{{Short description|Decidability assumption}}
The '''decisional composite residuosity assumption (DCRA)''' is a mathematical assumption used in [[cryptography]]. In particular, the assumption is used in the proof of the [[Paillier cryptosystem]].

Informally, the DCRA states that given a [[composite number|composite]] <math>n</math> and an [[integer]] <math>z</math>, it is hard to decide whether <math>z</math> is an <math>n</math>-residue [[modular arithmetic|modulo]] <math>n^2</math>. ''I.e.'' whether there exists a <math>y</math> such that

: <math>z \equiv y^n \pmod{n^2}. \, </math>
